qualification_limits: Global IBD and current incoming donor snapshots match for all six rows. Current donor annotations corroborate experimental grounding; their original papers were not newly read for this query.
No target-specific loss was found in retained family records; absence of a loss record is not proof that every ancestral function has been tested in the human protein.
The two target GO-CAM models reuse PMID40240600; they are curatorial models, not independent experiments.

primary.reading: Human H1.4 chromatosomes were reconstituted separately from other H1 proteins and chimeras; structural contacts do not identify a cellular division stage.
Full-length human P10412 was added to preassembled nucleosome arrays; structural incorporation is distinct from assembling the initial core octamer.
Human H1.4 DNA-binding, chromatin-fraction and compaction experiments distinguish wild-type protein from modification-site mutants.
Indexed original Results support preferential heterochromatin localization of human H1.4 fusions in mouse cells. Complete Methods were unavailable.
primary.capture_type: Preserved indexed original article text in web search response; full page inaccessible

primary.reading: The authentic abstract supports a nuclear histone-reader complex; full-paper access remained unavailable.
Human H1.4 nuclear distribution varies with cellular context. The paper warns that its phospho-T146 antibody may recognize other H1 proteins.
Human H1.4-dependent mitotic compaction and direct nucleosome binding coexist with dissociation of the S35-phosphorylated pool.
